headline: bdnews24.com Editor-in-Chief Toufique Imrose Khalidi dies at 59
summary: The veteran journalist, who pioneered digital news in Bangladesh, passed away in London after suffering a brain haemorrhage.
details: Toufique Imrose Khalidi, the Editor-in-Chief of bdnews24.com, passed away at 59 on Friday. He was pronounced dead at 2:23 pm London time after suffering a brain haemorrhage.
Khalidi had been on a personal visit to London when he suddenly fell ill and was admitted to St Bartholomew's Hospital on Thursday night.
He is remembered as a pioneer who brought Bangladesh's news services into the digital world, with colleagues describing him as a journalist who never let news stray from objectivity.
BNP Acting Secretary General Ruhul Kabir Rizvi called him an 'honest and courageous journalist who set an example in his work.'
President Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir and several government ministers, including the Information Minister and Finance Minister, expressed their grief and condolences over the loss.
caption:
A pioneer of digital journalism in Bangladesh has passed away. Toufique Imrose Khalidi died at 59 in London.

Toufique Imrose Khalidi, the Editor-in-Chief of bdnews24.com, passed away at 59 on Friday. He was pronounced dead at 2:23 pm London time after suffering a brain haemorrhage.

Khalidi had been on a personal visit to London when he suddenly fell ill and was admitted to St Bartholomew's Hospital on Thursday night.

He is remembered as a pioneer who brought Bangladesh's news services into the digital world, with colleagues describing him as a journalist who never let news stray from objectivity.

BNP Acting Secretary General Ruhul Kabir Rizvi called him an 'honest and courageous journalist who set an example in his work.'

President Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir and several government ministers, including the Information Minister and Finance Minister, expressed their grief and condolences over the loss.

headline_marked: Jamaat leader [[Akhtaruzzaman arrested]] over alleged airport assault
headline: Jamaat leader Akhtaruzzaman arrested over alleged airport assault
summary: The former MP and freedom fighter was detained following a viral video showing him arguing with airport officials over Zamzam water distribution.
details: Jamaat-e-Islami leader and former MP Mohammad Aktaruzzaman Ranjan was arrested at his home in Dhaka’s Cantonment on Friday evening.
The arrest follows a case filed by a security officer of the Civil Aviation Authority of Bangladesh (CAAB) over alleged threats and assault at Shahjalal International Airport.
The incident occurred after a viral video showed Akhtaruzzaman remonstrating over delays in distributing Zamzam water to Umrah pilgrims arriving from Madinah.
In the video, he is heard threatening the airport's Executive Director, Ragib Samad, saying, 'I'll grab you by the collar and throw you out.'
Jamaat-e-Islami has condemned the arrest, calling it a 'flimsy pretext' and demanding his immediate release.
The party's Secretary General, Mia Golam Porwar, called for an impartial probe into the mismanagement and harassment faced by passengers at the airport.
Jamaat's Dhaka North unit also held a rally and marched from Uttara's Jashimuddin Road to Airport Road to protest the detention.
Party leaders described Akhtaruzzaman as a celebrated freedom fighter and war veteran, arguing that the case was filed out of anger after he spoke against negligence.
caption:
A viral video of a heated argument at the airport leads to the arrest of a former MP.

Jamaat-e-Islami leader and former MP Mohammad Aktaruzzaman Ranjan was arrested at his home in Dhaka’s Cantonment on Friday evening.

The arrest follows a case filed by a security officer of the Civil Aviation Authority of Bangladesh (CAAB) over alleged threats and assault at Shahjalal International Airport.

The incident occurred after a viral video showed Akhtaruzzaman remonstrating over delays in distributing Zamzam water to Umrah pilgrims arriving from Madinah.

In the video, he is heard threatening the airport's Executive Director, Ragib Samad, saying, 'I'll grab you by the collar and throw you out.'

Jamaat-e-Islami has condemned the arrest, calling it a 'flimsy pretext' and demanding his immediate release.

The party's Secretary General, Mia Golam Porwar, called for an impartial probe into the mismanagement and harassment faced by passengers at the airport.

Jamaat's Dhaka North unit also held a rally and marched from Uttara's Jashimuddin Road to Airport Road to protest the detention.

Party leaders described Akhtaruzzaman as a celebrated freedom fighter and war veteran, arguing that the case was filed out of anger after he spoke against negligence.
